title: Garlicky Gochujang and Tomato Bucatini
changes_from_base: The butter-onion tomato sauce is replaced by passata simmered with a whole head of garlic and gochujang, then finished with ricotta and basil.
summary: Bucatini in a sweet, garlicky passata sauce spiked with gochujang, topped with cool ricotta and torn basil.
equipment: large frying pan or sauté pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: fine salt for 3 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 4 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Garlic oil
steps.text: Put the oil and sliced garlic into the cold pan and set it over medium-low heat. Cook 5-7 min, stirring now and then, until the slices are soft and only just turning pale gold; starting cold stops the garlic burning before it has softened.

steps.title: Bloom the gochujang
steps.text: Stir in the chilli paste and cook for 1 min until it loosens and turns a shade darker, which deepens its fermented sweetness.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in the passata, bring to a gentle bubble and cook 8-10 min until slightly thickened. Turn the heat down if it spits. Set aside off the heat.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Bring 3 litres water to the boil with the salt and cook the bucatini until al dente. Scoop out a mug of the water, then drain.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Warm the sauce again, add the pasta and about 100 ml of the water and toss for 1 min until the sauce clings inside and out. Taste before adding any more salt, as gochujang is already salty.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide between bowls and top each with a spoonful of ricotta, black pepper and torn basil. The cool ricotta softens the chilli heat.

tips: Slice the garlic thinly and evenly so it softens at the same rate.
Gochujang brands vary in heat and salt; start with 2 tbsp if yours is fiery.
Lower the heat if the sauce spits, since passata catches easily.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C).
